Layer the fillets with garlic and parsley; cover with the oil.

Fry at 175 °C, 2–3 min, in small batches, until golden and core 63 °C.
Drain, salt at once and serve with 25 g lemon wedges.

Add the wine and reduce until absorbed.
Add the hot stock in stages, stirring, for 16–18 min until the rice is cooked but slightly firm.
Off the heat, beat in the butter, Parmesan, salt and pepper.
Spread 3 cm deep on lined GN trays; cool to \< 10 °C within 90 min (blast chiller).
Sweat the onion in the oil for 2–3 min.
Add the mince and brown for 5 min, breaking it up.
Add the tomato sauce, salt and pepper; simmer 4 min until thick. Core ≥ 75 °C.
Scale 60 g of cold risotto base per ball and flatten in the palm.

Fry at 175 °C for 4–5 min until golden. Core ≥ 75 °C; if lower, finish at 180 °C convection for 4–5 min.

Poach in water with bay leaves at 85–90 °C for 10–15 min, to a core of 63 °C.
While warm, beat the flesh, adding the oil in a thin stream, to a smooth emulsion.
Season with garlic, white pepper, lemon juice; add salt only if needed after tasting.

Season with the sea salt and pepper; dot with the olive oil and balsamic.

Vacuum-pack with the thyme, garlic and oil.
Cook sous-vide at 56 °C for 4 h (core 56 °C held for at least 2 h).
Chill in an ice bath to below 5 °C core within 90 min. Refrigerate at least 12 h before slicing.

Pinbone and trim the fillets; keep at 0–2 °C.
Just before service, slice 3 mm thin on a chilled plate, 90 g per portion.
Season with sea salt, pepper, 3.5 g lemon juice and zest and 7 g olive oil. Serve immediately.
5aeef238.st: Thawed fillet: 0–2 °C, 24 h. Sliced fish: serve immediately, do not store.

Emulsion: olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Brush bresaola lightly; top with 20 g dressed rocket and 15 g Parmesan shavings; lemon wedge.
af1d6352.st: Sliced bresaola dries fast: slice to order, 0–4 °C.

Mix with olive oil, torn basil, a little crushed garlic, oregano and pepper. Make no more than 1 h before service.
Slice bread 1.5 cm (30 slices × 30 g); grill or char-grill 1–2 min per side.
Rub hot toast with cut garlic; brush with oil.
Top with 30 g tomato per slice at the pass (bread stays crisp); flaky salt, basil leaf.
af227ee0.st: Topping: 0–4 °C, 4 h max (tomatoes go watery). Toast to order.

Cover the peppers for 10 min to steam; peel and remove the seeds and stalks.
Blend the pepper flesh and roasted garlic, emulsifying in the oil; season with the salt. Pass through a sieve.
Take the burrata out 20–30 min before service (12–14 °C).
Spread 115 g crema di peperoni on the plate; place one burrata on top.
Finish with 3 g olive oil and black pepper. Serve at once.

Dress with the olive oil and capers. Keep at 0–4 °C.
Take the burrata out of the fridge 20–30 min before service to reach 12–14 °C; never longer than 30 min.
Plate 85 g peppers, 1 burrata on top, 12 g anchovy fillets and fresh basil.
Season the burrata with a little sea salt.
adfbd312.st: Dressed peppers: 0–4 °C, 72 h. Burrata: 0–4 °C, supplier's date. Opened anchovies: 0–4 °C under oil, 5 days. Do not freeze.

Cut the figs into quarters just before service.

Toss in the flour per order (about 210 g squid per portion); shake off the excess.
Fry at 175 °C, 2 min, in small batches, until golden and core 63 °C.
Drain, salt at once and serve with 25 g lemon wedges.
46673e24.st: Raw squid: 0–2 °C, 24 h (thaw frozen at 0–4 °C). Fried: serve immediately. Change frying oil per oil-quality test.

Chop the squid tentacles finely; sauté them in 20 g of the oil with the garlic 2 min. Cool.
Mix the crumbs, Parmigiano, parsley, tentacle mixture, remaining oil and salt into a moist, loose stuffing. Chill to 0–4 °C before filling.

Fill each tube two-thirds full (the stuffing swells); close with a cocktail stick.
Season with the salt. Sear in a hot pan in the oil, 1 min per side, until coloured.
Finish in a convection oven at 180 °C for 15–18 min to a core temperature of 63 °C. Do not overcook or the squid toughens.
Rest 2 min, remove the sticks, slice into 2 cm rounds or serve whole.
Plate 260 g per portion (about 3 stuffed squid). Serve at once.
525166b8.st: Stuffing: 0–4 °C, 24 h. Stuffed raw squid: 0–4 °C, 24 h; −18 °C, 1 month. Cooked: 0–4 °C, 48 h (reheat to 75 °C core).

Place 30 scallops (30 g) on cleaned half shells or small gratin dishes; season; splash of wine.
Cover each with 8 g crumb; drizzle oil.
Bake 230 °C top heat 5–6 min (core 50 °C, crumb golden). Lemon wedge.

Cut the peppers into 1.5 cm dice and the onion into fine dice.
Blanch the tomatoes 10–15 s, refresh in iced water, peel and dice. Slice the olives; rinse the capers.
Fry the aubergine in 100 g of the oil over medium-high heat for 5–7 min until golden; drain on paper.

Add the tomato paste and fry 1 min. Add the tomatoes, sugar, lemon juice, salt and pepper; simmer 5–7 min until thick.
Add the aubergine, olives and capers; simmer gently 5 min.

Sweat onion and celery in olive oil until translucent, 8 min.
Add tomatoes and sugar; simmer 8–10 min until thickened.
Add vinegar and reduce 3–4 min; add olives and capers; season.

Chop; mix with breadcrumbs, Pecorino, egg, garlic, basil; season; firm enough to roll (add crumbs if wet).
Roll 40 balls × 30 g; coat in breadcrumbs; fry 175 °C 3 min (or bake 200 °C 15 min, oiled).

8f9182b7.st: Shaped raw: 0–4 °C, 24 h. Fried: 0–4 °C, 48 h; reheat 180 °C 6 min.

Toast the walnuts in a dry pan 2–3 min; cool, break roughly.
Arrange the rocket on a flat plate; drape the prosciutto in loose folds; add the figs.
Finish with parmesan shavings and walnuts; dress just before service.
fa88ce8a.st: Dressing: 0–4 °C, 5 days. Cut figs: 0–4 °C, 12 h. Assembled salad: serve immediately. Do not freeze.

Heat the griddle to about 220 °C and oil it lightly.
Cook the cheese 1–2 min per side until a golden crust forms and the centre softens.
Plate and finish with 12 g honey, lemon zest and black pepper. Serve at once.
787ca5da.st: Provola, cut: 0–4 °C, wrapped, 5 days. Cooked: serve immediately, do not store.

c: Drain the ricotta in a cloth-lined sieve overnight at 0–4 °C.
Mix in half the herbs (thyme, rosemary, oregano), the salt and the pepper.
Press into oiled moulds or a lined GN 1/2 tray, 4 cm deep. Brush the top with 40 g of the oil.
Bake in a convection oven at 180 °C for 20 min, to a core temperature of 75 °C and a golden top.

f43c5cbd.st: Drained ricotta: 0–4 °C, 48 h. Baked: 0–4 °C, 72 h; reheat at 160 °C to 75 °C core. Do not freeze.

Shave the Parmesan. Chop the walnuts coarsely.
Core the pear and slice thinly to order to prevent browning.
Arrange the rocket on chilled plates (50 g); lay the prosciutto over it (25 g).
Add the pear and walnuts; drizzle with the dressing (22 g).

Toss rocket and tomatoes with oil, balsamic, salt and pepper.
Plate; add 2 slices of prosciutto; finish with parmesan shavings.
Serve immediately with the ciabatta (≈135 g).
85d4472e.st: Assembled salad: serve immediately. Sliced prosciutto: 0–4 °C, 48 h.

Bake the cheese, convection 180 °C, 10–12 min, until fully melted and lightly golden.
Finish with 7 g olive oil and black pepper. Serve at once in the dish with the bruschetta.
4b309b55.st: Scamorza, whole: 0–4 °C, supplier's date; cut: 0–4 °C, 5 days, wrapped. Baked: serve immediately, do not store.

Toast on the grill or in the oven, convection 200 °C, 4–5 min, until crisp.
Take the stracciatella out of the fridge 20–30 min before service to reach 12–14 °C; never longer than 30 min.
Plate 125 g per portion. Season with the sea salt and black pepper.
Finish with 10 g olive oil and 3 g truffle oil per portion. Serve with the warm bruschetta.
2736f78b.st: Stracciatella: 0–4 °C, within supplier's date, max 48 h once opened. Toasted bread: airtight, room temperature, same day. Do not freeze.

Take the stracciatella out 20–30 min before service (12–14 °C).
Spoon 100 g stracciatella onto a cold plate; add 60 g dressed tomatoes and 10 g anchovy fillets.
Finish with 6 g olive oil and black pepper. Serve at once.

c: Toast the rice 2 min in a dry pan. Add the tomato sauce and the hot water in stages, stirring, 16–18 min, until thick and just cooked.
Season with the salt. Spread 3 cm deep on a tray and cool to below 5 °C within 90 min (blast chiller).
Shape 63 g of cold rice around 10 g mozzarella into oval croquettes.
Coat in flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs. Keep at 0–4 °C until frying.
Fry at 170–175 °C, 4–5 min, until golden and core 75 °C.
Drain on paper and serve hot, 3 pieces per portion.
b89413d9.st: Cooked rice: 0–4 °C, 24 h. Breaded raw supplì: 0–4 °C, 48 h; −18 °C, 1 month (fry from frozen at 165 °C to core 75 °C). Fried: serve immediately. Change frying oil per oil-quality test.
b89413d9.al: 1 Gluten (wheat) · 3 Eggs · 7 Milk (tomato sauce: check recipe/label)

c: Season the turkey with the salt; tie into an even roll if needed.
Poach in water held at 80 °C (no boiling) for 60–75 min to a core temperature of 75 °C.
Cool in the liquid to 60 °C, then blast-chill to below 5 °C within 90 min.
Slice thinly (3 mm) on the slicer.
Blend the tuna, capers, lemon juice and salt until smooth.
Fold in the mayonnaise. Adjust consistency with up to 30 g of the poaching liquid. Chill at 0–4 °C.
Fan 105 g sliced turkey on a cold plate; coat with 90 g tonnato sauce.
Garnish with 3 g capers. Serve at 4–8 °C.
cb0bda55.st: Cooked turkey: 0–4 °C, 72 h; −18 °C, 2 months. Tonnato sauce: 0–4 °C, 48 h; do not freeze. Plated: 0–4 °C, max. 12 h.

c: Toast the walnuts at 160 °C convection for 8–10 min; chop roughly.
Cut the Taleggio into 125 g portions (rind on) and place each in an individual ovenproof dish brushed with 5 g olive oil.
Bake at 180 °C convection for 10–12 min until soft and molten.
Finish each with 15 g honey, 19 g walnuts and thyme leaves. Serve at once with bread.
123a974b.st: Taleggio: 0–4 °C, wrapped, 7 days after cutting. Toasted walnuts: airtight, 2 weeks. Bake to order.

Roast in a convection oven at 180 °C for 6–8 min until just soft.
Toast dry in a convection oven at 160 °C for 8–10 min until fragrant. Chop coarsely.
Cook to order · 100 g per portion
Cut 100 g pieces; temper for no more than 30 min (to 16–18 °C).
Place each in an individual ovenproof dish; bake at 180 °C for 8–10 min until soft and starting to run, but still holding its shape.
Top with 60 g pears, 15 g walnuts, 12 g honey, 4 g olive oil, black pepper and 0.75 g salt flakes. Serve at once.
6a48c2cc.st: Taleggio, cut and wrapped: 0–4 °C, 7 days. Roasted pears: 0–4 °C, 24 h. Walnuts: airtight, ambient, 2 weeks. Baked cheese: serve immediately.

c: Whisk the mustard, lemon juice, salt and pepper; emulsify in the olive oil; add the capers.
Use whole-muscle fillet from an approved supplier. Trim all sinew and surface; keep at 0–2 °C.
Per order, chop 147 g of beef finely with a knife on a chilled board.
Mix with 35 g dressing just before plating (lemon 'cooks' the meat if added early).
7dacfd22.st: Trimmed fillet: 0–2 °C, 48 h. Dressing: 0–4 °C, 5 days. Chopped tartare: made to order, never stored. Do not freeze after preparing.

c: Bring the water with celery, bay leaf and salt to 80–85 °C.
Add the veal and poach at 80–85 °C (no boil) 90–120 min to core 70 °C.
Cool in iced water / blast chiller to below 4 °C within 90 min. Keep 100 g of the poaching liquid for the sauce.
Blend tuna, anchovies, capers and lemon juice until smooth.
With the blender running, add the olive oil in a thin stream, then fold in the mayonnaise.
Adjust the consistency with poaching liquid. Keep at 0–4 °C.
Slice the chilled veal 2 mm thick on a slicer; 160 g per portion on a chilled plate.
Coat with 120 g sauce; garnish with 5 g capers and parsley.
Rest at 0–4 °C for 2 h for the flavours to develop; serve at 4–8 °C.

Shallow-fry in the olive oil at 170 °C, in batches, until golden. Drain and salt.
Layer in a GN with the garlic and torn mint, sprinkling each layer with the vinegar.
Cover and marinate at 0–4 °C for at least 4 h.
Take out 30 min before service; serve 130 g per portion, at room temperature for max 2 h.
fc7f37ce.st: 0–4 °C, 72 h (contains raw garlic in oil – keep chilled). Do not freeze.

Add crushed tomatoes, chilli; 10 min; add stock; simmer 20 min; season.
Poach 10 eggs in the simmering soup 3–4 min (or separately).
Toast in each bowl, grated Pecorino, soup and 1 egg on top; basil, raw oil.

Crushed tomatoes and stock; simmer 30 min (octopus tender).
Add hake, then prawns, then mussels and clams; cover; cook 5–6 min until shells open, fish 63 °C core. Parsley.
Grill 10 thick slices; rub with garlic, oil; lay in the bowl and ladle the stew over.

Add the stock, bay and thyme; simmer gently about 20 min until the vegetables start to soften.
Add the beans and ditalini; simmer until the pasta is al dente, 8–10 min.

Off the heat: torn basil, season; rest 10 min.
Serve warm or at room temperature with raw olive oil (50 g) and basil.

Cook ditalini in the soup 9–10 min, stirring often (it catches).
Season; finish with chilli and raw olive oil.
Render diced pancetta in oil; add soffritto (onion, carrot, celery, fine dice) and garlic, sweat 10 min.
Add crushed tomatoes, beans, stock, rosemary and bay; simmer 20 min.
Blend one third of the soup and return (creamy body, no cream).

Serve with grated Parmesan and a thread of raw olive oil.

Pour in the egg mix in a thin stream while stirring gently to form fine strands.
Return to a simmer (core 75 °C); season and serve at once.

Add lentils, crushed tomatoes, hot stock, bay and rosemary; simmer 35–40 min until tender; salt at the end.

Heat the oil; sweat shallot and garlic without colour.

Add garlic 1 min, then mince; brown on high heat, breaking up, until liquid evaporates (8 min).

Blanch the tomatoes 15 s, refresh in iced water, peel and deseed.
Grind the almonds with the garlic, then the basil and tomatoes, to a coarse paste. Add the Parmesan and oil to a creamy texture; season with the salt. Keep at 0–4 °C.
Cook the busiate in water salted at 10 g/L until al dente (100 g dry per portion).

Whisk in the hot milk (80 °C) gradually; simmer 8–10 min, stirring, until smooth and thick.
Season with the salt and nutmeg. Cover the surface with film. Use hot, or cool to below 5 °C within 90 min.
Wilt the spinach in a hot pan 2–3 min; cool, squeeze dry and chop.
Mix with the ricotta and the salt. Keep at 0–4 °C.
Spread a thin layer of béchamel in the GN trays.
Pipe the filling into the dry tubes and lay them side by side, 8 per portion.
Cover completely with béchamel (the tubes must be fully covered to cook) and sprinkle with parmesan.

Serve 300 g per portion. Reheat to core 75 °C; hot-hold at 63 °C or above.

c: Bring 10 L water to the boil with the salt (10 g per litre).
Cook the pasta until al dente. Reserve 200 g of the cooking water; drain.
Season the chicken with 10 g of the salt and the pepper.
Sear in the oil over medium-high heat until golden and cooked to a core of 75 °C. Remove and reserve.
In the same pan, melt the butter and cook the garlic for 30 s without colour.
Add the cream and bring to a gentle simmer.
Whisk in the Parmesan until melted and smooth; season with the remaining salt.
Add the chicken and pasta; toss to coat. Adjust the consistency with the pasta water.
Finish with the parsley and serve at once, above 63 °C.
58e1745c.st: Cooked chicken: 0–4 °C, 48 h. Finished dish: serve immediately; do not hold or reheat.

c: Bring 4 L water to the boil with the salt (10 g per litre).
Cook the linguine until al dente; reserve 100 g of the cooking water.
Keep the seafood at 0–4 °C until cooking. Scrub and de-beard the mussels; discard any that stay open when tapped.
Heat the oil and butter. Sear the shrimp, squid and scallops for 1 min; remove and reserve.
Sweat the shallot for 2–3 min; add the garlic and cook for 30 s.
Add the mussels and the wine; cover and cook until the mussels open, 2–3 min. Discard any that stay closed. Reduce the liquid by half.
Add the cream and simmer gently for 2–3 min. Stir in the Parmesan until smooth.
Return the seared seafood; heat through to a core of 63 °C.
Add the linguine and enough pasta water for a silky, emulsified sauce.
Finish with the lemon zest, juice, parsley and pepper; correct the salt. Serve at once.

Sauce: onion in oil, crushed tomatoes, salt; simmer 25 min; basil.

Add cream, simmer 3 min; add salmon in 2 cm cubes and poach 3 min (core ≥ 63 °C) without stirring hard.
Finish with lemon zest, juice and dill; season.
Cook farfalle al dente; toss gently with the sauce and spinach until it wilts; serve at once.

Cut fettuccine 6 mm; boil 2 min in lightly salted water.
In a warm bowl or pan off the heat: soft butter (30 g) and finely grated 24-month Parmigiano (30 g) per portion.
Add pasta with 40 g cooking water; toss hard 30–40 s until a creamy emulsion forms (no cream, no heat).

Sweat tomatoes in oil 3 min; add fregola; cook risotto-style with clam juice and hot stock 12–14 min.
Add clams (in shell and picked), chilli; 1 min; parsley, raw oil. Slightly soupy.

Cook in a separate, clean pot
Use a dedicated pot, colander and utensils (no contact with wheat pasta water).

Off the heat, add the gorgonzola in pieces and stir until melted and smooth. Hold at 63–70 °C.
Toast the walnuts at 160 °C convection 8–10 min; cool and chop roughly.
Bring the salted water to the boil. Cook the gnocchi 2–3 min, until they float; drain.
Toss 175 g of gnocchi with 150 g of gorgonzola sauce for 30 s over heat.
Plate and finish with 25 g of toasted walnuts. Serve at once (≥ 63 °C).

Cook on low heat 8–10 min, stirring with a spatula, until it leaves the sides of the pot.
Off the heat: beat in yolks and 100 g Parmesan.
Spread 1 cm thick on an oiled tray; cool and set 2 h at 0–4 °C. Cut 6 cm discs.
Overlap discs in buttered dishes; melted butter (60 g) and Parmesan (80 g) on top.
Bake 200 °C 15–20 min until golden; serve at ≥ 75 °C.

Bring the tomato sauce to a simmer; season with the salt.
Blanch the gnocchi in boiling salted water until they float (1–2 min); lift out and drain well.
Toss the gnocchi with the hot sauce and the olive oil; spread into 2 oiled GN 1/1 trays.
Scatter the mozzarella and parmesan evenly over the top.
Bake at 200 °C convection for 12–15 min until bubbling and golden; core 75 °C.
Rest 5 min and portion 300 g; hold hot at ≥ 63 °C for max 2 h.

Mix with drained ricotta, Parmesan, eggs, flour, nutmeg, salt.
Shape 60 balls × 30 g; roll in semolina; tray on semolina, chill 12 h (forms a skin).
Poach in gently simmering salted water 3–4 min until they float + 1 min.
Toss in foaming sage butter; Parmesan.
72e0c5dd.al: 1 Gluten (wheat flour, coarse semolina) · 3 Eggs (eggs) · 7 Milk (ricotta, parmesan, butter). Vegetarian (check rennet).

Sauté the mushrooms in the olive oil in batches over high heat until all liquid has evaporated; season with the salt. Cool to below 10 °C.
Spread a thin layer of béchamel in the GN tray.
Build 5 layers: pasta sheets, mushrooms, béchamel, a little parmesan. Finish with béchamel and the remaining parmesan.
Cover with foil and bake at 180 °C convection for 20 min; uncover and bake a further 15 min until golden; core 75 °C.

Slice potatoes 2 mm and cut beans 2 cm; blanch together 3 min.
Mix 400 g béchamel with the pesto (keep the colour: do not heat the pesto separately).
Layer: béchamel, sheets, pesto-béchamel, potatoes and beans, Parmesan × 5 layers; finish with béchamel and Parmesan.

c: Simmer the shells from the prawns in the water 20 min; strain (≈ 300 g). Keep hot.
Clean the mussels (remove beards; discard any open that do not close when tapped). Halve the tomatoes; slice the garlic and chilli.
Cook the pasta in boiling water salted at 10 g/L until al dente; reserve some cooking water. Linguine 8–10 min.
Steam the mussels in a covered pan with 30 g of the wine 3–4 min until open; discard any that stay closed. Shell most of them; strain and keep the liquor.
Sweat the garlic and chilli in 40 g oil 1 min without colour. Add the remaining wine and reduce 1–2 min; add the tomatoes and cook 3 min.
Add 250 g stock and the mussel liquor; simmer 3 min. Add the prawns and squid and cook 2 min to a core of 63 °C. Season with salt and pepper.
Add the drained pasta, mussels and lemon zest; toss. Off the heat, finish with the butter and remaining oil, loosening with pasta water.
Serve at once with the parsley and Parmesan.

Garlic and chilli in oil 1 min; halved tomatoes 2 min; white wine, reduce.
Boil linguine 2 min less than the pack time; finish in the pan with pasta water 2 min.
Off the heat fold in crab (only warmed, stays sweet), parsley, lemon zest, raw oil.
4e494931.st: Crab meat: 0–2 °C, per label; finish to order.

Melt the butter with the oil over low heat.
Add the zest and warm gently 1 min without frying.
Add 1–2 ladles of pasta water and whisk hard to a creamy emulsion.
Add the pasta and the lemon juice.
Off the heat, at 65–70 °C, add the Parmesan and toss to a smooth, glossy sauce with no separated fat.
Season with salt and white pepper; serve at once (100 g dry pasta per portion).

Roll ropes 8 mm; cut 1.5 cm; roll each on a gnocchi board (ridged shells). Dry 2 h.
Brown crumbled sausage in oil; onion and garlic 5 min; wine, reduce.
Boil pasta 8–10 min; toss in ragù; 15 g pecorino per portion.

Warm the oil with the garlic and chilli over low heat; add the anchovies and stir until dissolved.
Cook the orecchiette in water salted at 10 g/L until al dente (100 g dry per portion).
Finish the pasta with the greens and the anchovy oil, loosening with cooking water. Adjust with the salt and serve at once.

Blanch the cime di rapa in boiling salted water 2 min; refresh in iced water, drain and chop.
Brown the crumbled sausage in 50 g oil, breaking it up, to a core of 75 °C.
Add the garlic and chilli for 1 min, then the cime di rapa; sauté 2–3 min. Season with the salt.
Cook the orecchiette in water salted at 10 g/L until al dente (100 g dry per portion). Finish in the sauce with cooking water to an emulsion.

c: Sweat the onion and garlic in the cooking oil for 8 min without colour.
Add the cherry tomatoes; cook for 5 min until they begin to break down.
Deglaze with the wine and reduce by half. Add the passata, sugar and stock; simmer for 12 min.
Cook the orzo in boiling salted water (10 g per litre) 1 min under the packet time.

Sweat the garlic in the oil without colour. Sear the seafood 1–2 min on high heat; remove and keep aside.
Add the wine and reduce by half; add the crushed tomatoes and salt and simmer 15 min.
Return the seafood with its juices and cook 2 min to a core of 63 °C.

Heat gradually over medium heat until the fat has rendered and the guanciale is golden.
Deglaze with the wine and reduce.
Add the crushed tomatoes, chilli and salt; reduce at a gentle simmer 8–10 min.
Cook the pasta in water salted at 10 g/L until al dente (100 g dry per portion); transfer to the sauce with some cooking water and toss to a glossy sauce.

Sweat pancetta and vegetables in oil 5 min; lay beef on top, then all the onions; salt; cover.
Cook covered on the lowest heat 3 h, stirring every 20 min (onions melt, no colour at first).
Uncover, add wine in stages over 1 h until onions are deep golden and jammy.
Shred beef into the sauce (or serve as a second course, Naples way); season.
Boil paccheri (or spezzati ziti) 2 min less than the pack time.

Cut the guanciale into 1 × 2 cm strips; render from a cold pan over medium heat until golden. Keep the fat.
Cook the pasta in lightly salted water (the 25 g salt for about 15 L) until al dente (100 g dry per portion).
Finish the pasta in the guanciale fat with the pepper and some cooking water.

c: Slice the zucchini into 3 mm rounds; salt lightly and dry.
Fry in olive oil at 160–170 °C in batches until golden; drain. Keep the flavoured oil.
Cook in boiling salted water 8–10 min until al dente; keep 400 g of the cooking water.
Per 2 portions in a wide pan: zucchini, a little zucchini oil and 80 g pasta water; warm through.
Off the heat add the drained pasta and two thirds of the grated provolone; toss to a creamy emulsion, 1–2 min.

Sweat the garlic in olive oil 1 min without colour.
Add the crushed tomatoes; simmer 10–12 min until thick. Season with salt, pepper and sugar; add half the basil at the end.
Cook the rigatoni in salted boiling water (10 g salt per litre) to al dente; keep 100 g of the cooking water.

4d6c1e00.st: Dough balls: 4 °C, use day 3–4. Toppings: 0–4 °C, 48 h.
4d6c1e00.al: 1 Gluten (tipo 00 flour) · 7 Milk (mozzarella fior di latte)

c: Roast or poach the chicken fillet to a core temperature of 75 °C; chill to below 5 °C within 90 min.
Shred or cut into small pieces. Keep at 0–4 °C (max. 48 h).
Mix the passata with 5 g of the olive oil, the salt and the oregano.
Slice the mushrooms 2–3 mm; drain the sweetcorn; slice the olives.
Place the base on a tray lined with baking paper; spread the sauce, leaving a 1–2 cm border.
Sprinkle with half the kashkaval; distribute the chicken, mushrooms, sweetcorn and olives; top with the remaining kashkaval.
Bake in a convection oven preheated to 220 °C for 12–15 min until golden; chicken topping must reach ≥75 °C.
60d0c5bb.st: Serve within 10 min of baking. If stored: cool to below 5 °C within 90 min, 0–4 °C max. 24 h; reheat in a convection oven at 180 °C to a core temperature of ≥75 °C.

21bf678e.yl: Yield: 10 pizzas Ø 30 cm · Portion: 1 pizza ≈ 440 g
c: Mix flour and 90 % of the water; autolyse 20 min. Add yeast, salt, rest of water, then oil.
Knead 10–12 min to smooth, dough temperature 23–24 °C; bulk 2 h at room temperature.
Ball 250 g; boxes, lidded; 72 h at 4 °C. Out 2–3 h before use (15–17 °C core).
Pick leaves and tender stems; blanch 1 min, chill, squeeze.
Sauté with garlic and chilli in oil 5 min until soft; season.
Stretch base; no tomato. Diced provola 90 g, friarielli 60 g.
Skinned sausage pinched in small pieces, 70 g; Parmesan.
Bake 430–450 °C 80–90 s (sausage 72 °C core; deck oven 300 °C 6 min); olive oil.
21bf678e.al: 1 Gluten (tipo 00 flour) · 7 Milk (provola affumicata, parmesan). Friarielli can be replaced by cime di rapa or tenderstem.

91e670ad.yl: Yield: 10 pizzas Ø 30 cm · Portion: 1 pizza ≈ 450 g
c: Mix flour and 90 % of the water; autolyse 20 min. Add yeast, salt, rest of water, then oil.
Knead 10–12 min to smooth, dough temperature 23–24 °C; bulk 2 h at room temperature.
Ball 250 g; boxes, lidded; 72 h at 4 °C. Out 2–3 h before use (15–17 °C core).
Crush tomatoes by hand or pass through a food mill (no blender: aerates and turns orange); season. Raw, not cooked.
Slice onion 2 mm; soak 10 min in iced water, dry (milder).
Stretch; sauce 80 g, mozzarella 90 g, onion 40 g.
Bake 430–450 °C 70–80 s; flaked tuna 60 g and olives on after baking (stays moist); oregano, olive oil.

2633814c.yl: Yield: 10 pizzas Ø 30 cm · Portion: 1 pizza ≈ 520 g
c: 10 balls × 250 g (65% hydration, 24 h cold ferment)
Mix flour and 90% of the water 2 min; rest 20 min (autolyse).
Add yeast, then salt and remaining water; knead 8–10 min to a smooth dough (24–26 °C); add oil last.
Bulk 2 h at room temperature; divide 10 × 250 g, ball tightly, box and cold-ferment 24 h at 4 °C.
Take out 3 h before service; open by hand from the centre, leaving a 2 cm rim; never use a rolling pin.
Crush tomatoes by hand or pass through a food mill; do not cook.
Season with salt, oil, oregano and torn basil; hold 0–4 °C.
Slice zucchini and eggplant 5 mm, peppers in strips, onion in thin rings.
Toss with oil and salt; grill on hot plancha 1–2 min per side; cool on trays.
per pizza: 80 g sauce, 110 g mozzarella, 160 g vegetables
Spread sauce, add mozzarella, grilled vegetables, halved cherry tomatoes and olives.
Bake at 300–350 °C on the stone 90 s–2 min (deck 280 °C, 5–6 min) until the rim is leopard-spotted and the base crisp.
Finish with basil and a drizzle of oil.
2633814c.st: Grilled vegetables 0–4 °C 3 days. Bake to order.

0a33e609.yl: Yield: 10 portions · Portion: 250 g (on the bone)
c: Cut lamb in 60–70 g pieces on the bone (saw); dry; season.
Brown hard in oil in a wide rondeau, in batches; add half the garlic, rosemary and sage.
White wine, reduce; cover; braise 160 °C 1 h 15 min until tender (spoon-soft, 90 °C core).
Pestata: pound rest of garlic, rosemary leaves and anchovy with the vinegar; add in the last 10 min, uncovered, until glazed.
0a33e609.al: 4 Fish (anchovy fillets) · 14 Sulphites (white wine, white wine vinegar)

c: Score the skin in a crosshatch without cutting the meat. Season with salt and pepper.
Place skin side down in a cold pan; render over medium heat 8–10 min until the skin is crisp. Pour off the fat as it renders.
Turn and cook 2–3 min on the flesh side, to a core of 57 °C (pink). Cook to 75 °C on guest request.
Reduce the orange juice, white wine and brown sugar to a light syrup (about 400 g).
Off the heat, whisk in the cold butter a few pieces at a time. Hold at 60–65 °C; do not boil.
Slice the duck breast and fan it on a warm plate; nap with 50 g of orange sauce.
106e78e1.st: Raw duck breast: 0–4 °C, 48 h; −18 °C, 6 months. Orange sauce: 0–4 °C, 72 h; −18 °C, 2 months. Cooked duck: 0–4 °C, 48 h.

7367207d.yl: Yield: 10 portions · Portion: 180 g pork + 20 g jus = 200 g
c: Pound garlic, rosemary, fennel, salt and pepper to a paste; make deep slits in the loin and fill; rub the rest outside; tie.
Roast 220 °C 15 min, then 160 °C 50–60 min to 65 °C core; baste twice with wine and juices.
Rest 15 min (rises to 68 °C); slice 1 cm; deglaze the tray for jus. Serve warm or cold.
Tie the pork neck into an even roll.
Chop garlic and rosemary; rub the meat with salt, pepper, garlic, rosemary and part of the oil.
Sear on all sides in the remaining oil until golden.
Roast at 170 °C convection for 90–120 min, basting with the wine every 20 min, to core 72 °C.
Rest 15 min loosely covered, then slice 1 cm thick.
Strain and skim the roasting juices to serve as jus.
Serve 180 g sliced pork with 15 g jus per portion.
912d0bcb.st: Roast pork: 0–4 °C, 72 h; −18 °C, 3 months. Jus: 0–4 °C, 72 h. Regenerate to core 75 °C.

c: Soak the salt cod 48 h at 0–4 °C, changing the water every 8 h. Drain, pat dry and cut into 14 × 180 g pieces.
Sear the cod in half the olive oil, 1–2 min per side; set aside.
Sweat the garlic in the remaining olive oil 1 min. Add the crushed tomatoes, olives and capers; simmer 10 min.
Season the sauce with the salt and pepper.
Return the cod to the sauce and simmer on low heat 15–20 min, until the fish flakes and the sauce has reduced; core 63 °C.
650bfc62.st: Soaked salt cod: 0–4 °C, 48 h. Cooked dish: 0–4 °C, 48 h; −18 °C, 2 months. Regenerate to 75 °C core.

43219c64.yl: Yield: 10 portions · Portion: 180 g fish & sauce + 150 g polenta
c: Batch · soaked cod 1.8 kg → ≈ 1800 g with sauce
Soak salt cod 48–72 h in cold water at 4 °C, changing water every 8 h; skin, bone, cut 6 cm pieces.
Soften sliced onion in 100 g oil 15 min; melt anchovies in; add parsley.
Flour the cod; layer in a pan with onion sauce, Parmesan and pepper; cover with milk and remaining oil.
Cook very gently 2.5–3 h (barely simmering, 85–90 °C) without stirring; shake the pan.
Rain polenta into boiling salted water; cook 40–45 min stirring; serve soft or grilled.
43219c64.al: 1 Gluten (wheat flour) · 4 Fish (salt cod, anchovy fillets) · 7 Milk (milk 3%, parmesan)

c: Temper the steak out of the fridge for max. 30 min; pat dry.
Grill on very high heat (350–400 °C) 3–4 min per side to a deep crust; stand it on the bone 2–3 min.
For thick steaks finish at 180 °C convection to core 52–55 °C (rare / medium-rare).
Rest 5–8 min; season with salt, pepper, oil and rosemary; carve off the bone.
f161ca89.st: Raw steak (vacuum): 0–4 °C, 5 days; −18 °C, 6 months. Cooked: 0–4 °C, 48 h.

c: Put the brisket and tongue in the cold water and bring slowly to the boil; skim.
Add the vegetables and salt; simmer gently (90–95 °C) for 1.5 h.
Add the chicken legs and simmer a further 1–1.5 h, until all meats are tender; chicken core 75 °C.
Lift out the tongue, peel it while warm and return to the broth.
Slice the meats and serve 250 g mixed meats with 100 g hot broth and some vegetables; hold in broth at ≥ 63 °C.
8ff5433e.st: Meats in broth: 0–4 °C, 72 h; −18 °C, 3 months. Broth alone: 0–4 °C, 72 h. Cool from 63 °C to below 5 °C within 90 min; regenerate to 75 °C core.

bf9c9bd2.yl: Yield: 5 portions (1 fish each) · Portion: 640 g
c: Batch · 5 sea bass × 500 g, gutted and scaled
Rinse the fish, pat dry and make 2–3 shallow cuts in the skin on each side.
Season inside and out with the salt and pepper; fill the cavity with the garlic, half of the lemon (sliced) and the herbs.
Arrange the tomatoes, olives and capers in a GN tray; lay the fish on top.
Drizzle with the olive oil and white wine.
Bake at 200 °C convection for 15–18 min; core 63 °C at the thickest part.
Rest 2 min; finish with juice from the remaining lemon and serve at once.
bf9c9bd2.st: Raw prepared fish: 0–2 °C, 24 h; −18 °C, 3 months. Cooked to order; not stored.

c: Portion the sea bass into 14 × 180 g pieces; season with 15 g of the salt and the pepper. Keep at 0–4 °C.
Slice the potatoes 1–2 mm thick on a mandoline. Blanch 1 min in boiling water, cool and dry well.
Toss the potato slices with the olive oil, garlic, thyme and remaining salt.
Lay the fillets on a lined tray, skin side down; overlap the potato slices on top like scales.
Bake at 190 °C convection 18–20 min until the crust is crisp and golden; core of the fish 63 °C.
54187826.st: Portioned raw sea bass: 0–2 °C, 48 h; −18 °C, 3 months. Blanched potato slices: 0–4 °C, 24 h. Cooked dish: serve at once; not for storage.

3c2caf56.yl: Yield: 10 portions · Portion: 1 fish 400 g whole → ≈ 180 g fillet + oil
c: Per 2 fish: 1 kg salt · not eaten
Mix coarse salt with lightly beaten whites and water to a damp sand.
Gut, do NOT scale (scales protect the flesh); dry; lemon slices and herbs in the cavity.
Bed of 1 cm salt; fish on top; cover completely with 1.5 cm salt, pressing.
Bake 200 °C 25–30 min (400 g fish) to 55–58 °C core (probe through the crust).
Crack the crust at the table; lift skin; fillet; serve with olive oil and lemon.
3c2caf56.st: Raw fish 0–2 °C, 48 h. Bake to order.

c: Batch · Yield ≈ 2760 g (meat ≈ 1800 g + sauce ≈ 960 g)
Marinate the beef in the wine with the onion, carrot and celery for 12 h at 0–4 °C, covered.
Drain; keep the wine and vegetables separately. Pat the meat dry and season with the salt.
Sear the beef in the olive oil on all sides until deep brown; remove.
Sweat the marinade vegetables 8–10 min; add the marinade wine, bring to the boil and skim.
Return the beef, add the stock, cover and braise at 150 °C convection (or combi 150 °C, 30% steam) for 2.5–3 h, until fork-tender; core ≥ 90 °C.
Lift out the meat and rest 15 min. Pass the sauce through a fine sieve, pressing the vegetables, and reduce to a coating consistency.
Slice the meat 1 cm across the grain; serve 150 g meat with 80 g sauce, ≥ 63 °C.
794f7450.st: Braised meat in sauce: 0–4 °C, 72 h; −18 °C, 3 months. Raw meat in marinade: 0–4 °C, max 24 h. Cool from 63 °C to below 5 °C within 90 min; regenerate to 75 °C core.

f7ade855.yl: Yield: 10 portions · Portion: 350 g (on the bone, with sauce)
c: Raw oxtail 4 kg → ≈ 2200 g on the bone · Yield ≈ 3500 g
Soak oxtail 2 h in cold water; dry; season; brown hard in oil in batches.
Render guanciale; onion, carrot, 200 g celery 10 min; return oxtail; red wine, reduce.
Tomatoes and cloves; cover; braise 150 °C 3.5–4 h until meat falls off the bone.
Blanch the remaining celery in 5 cm sticks 3 min; add with raisins, pine nuts and cocoa; simmer 20 min; season.
Skim fat (or chill overnight and lift it).
Marinate the chops in the olive oil, garlic and rosemary for 2–12 h at 0–4 °C.
Take the chops out of the fridge 20 min before cooking (no longer than 30 min at room temperature). Season with salt and pepper.
Grill on a very hot grill (250–280 °C) 2–3 min per side; core 57 °C for medium-rare.
Rest 5 min before serving; serve straight away.
ec2f6d9e.st: Marinated raw chops: 0–4 °C, 48 h; raw chops −18 °C, 6 months. Cooked chops: 0–4 °C, 48 h.

c: Flatten the cutlets to 8–10 mm; season with the salt.
Bread in flour, then egg, then crumbs; press the crumbs on firmly. Keep at 0–4 °C until frying.
Heat the clarified butter and olive oil to 165–170 °C.
Fry 3–4 min per side until deep golden; core 70 °C.
Drain on a rack and serve at once.
163cadea.st: Raw breaded cutlets: 0–4 °C, 24 h; −18 °C, 1 month. Fried cutlets are not stored. Discard beaten egg after service.

eb8602e0.yl: Yield: 8 portions (¼ bird each) · Portion: 315 g

Brown all over in the olive oil in a roasting tray.
Roast at 170 °C convection for 60–75 min, basting every 15 min; add the wine after 20 min.
Check core 75 °C at the thickest part of the thigh.
Rest 10 min, joint into quarters and serve with the strained pan juices.
eb8602e0.st: Raw birds: 0–4 °C, 48 h. Roast guinea fowl: 0–4 °C, 48 h; −18 °C, 2 months. Regenerate to 75 °C core.

c: Dice the bread into 1 cm cubes.
Mix the mince, bread, eggs and salt until bound. Keep at 0–4 °C.
Partly bone the guinea fowl (remove the breastbone and backbone, leave the leg bones). Season inside and out with salt and pepper.
Fill each bird with the stuffing, roll and tie with kitchen string.
Brush with olive oil and place in a roasting tray; pour the white wine into the tray.
Roast at 170 °C convection (or combi 160 °C, 30 % humidity) about 75 min, basting with the tray juices every 20 min, until the core of the stuffing reaches 75 °C.
Rest 10 min, remove the string, slice and serve with the strained tray juices.

Sear the liver in batches in the remaining oil over high heat for 1–2 min; core 70 °C.
Deglaze with the white wine, return the onions and toss 1 min; season with the remaining salt and the pepper.
Serve at once at ≥ 63 °C; do not hold or reheat.

Heat the oil in an ovenproof pan; sweat the shallot until soft.
Add the pepper and cook 2–3 min; add the spinach and let it wilt.
Stir in the chopped sun-dried tomatoes.
Pour over the egg mixture and spread evenly; top with torn mozzarella.
Bake at 180 °C convection for 10–14 min until just set; core 72 °C.
d9cd0ae3.st: 0–4 °C, 48 h; −18 °C, 1 month. Serve hot or at room temperature within 2 h.

Beat the eggs with the Parmesan, salt and pepper.
Mix in the courgettes and pour into a lined, oiled GN 1/1 × 65 mm.
Bake at 170 °C convection (or combi 160 °C, 30 % humidity) 25–30 min, until set in the centre; core 75 °C.
Rest 10 min, cut into 14 portions. Serve hot (≥ 63 °C) or chilled.
74341f42.st: Baked frittata: 0–4 °C, 48 h; −18 °C, 1 month. Regenerate to 75 °C core.

Heat the oil to 175–180 °C. Load the fryer to max 30% of its capacity.
Just before frying, whisk the flour, corn starch and iced sparkling water briefly; small lumps are fine. Keep the batter on ice.
Dip the pieces in the batter, let the excess drip off and fry in small batches until light golden: squid 60–90 s, prawns about 60 s, courgette 1–2 min; seafood core 63 °C.
Drain on a rack, season at once with the sea salt and serve immediately.

91e2ab6e.st: Raw prepared seafood: 0–2 °C, 24 h. Fried product is not stored. Batter: max 2 h on ice.

c: Rinse the lentils; simmer in the water 25–30 min until tender but whole. Add 15 g of the salt for the last 5 min. Drain.
Sweat the onion, carrot and celery in the olive oil 10 min, until soft.
Fold the vegetables into the lentils; season with the remaining salt and the pepper. Hold at ≥ 63 °C.
Cut the guanciale into 1 × 4 cm strips.
Render in a dry pan over medium heat 10–12 min until crisp; drain on paper.
Spoon 330 g of lentils into a warm bowl; top with 33 g of crisp guanciale.
f2881293.st: Cooked lentils: 0–4 °C, 72 h; −18 °C, 3 months. Crisp guanciale: 0–4 °C, 5 days. Regenerate lentils to 75 °C core.

Cover each with prosciutto (about 21 g) and cheese (about 28 g); roll tightly and tie with string, seam side down.
Sear the rolls in the olive oil until golden on all sides.
Deglaze with the white wine and reduce by half.
Finish at 180 °C convection for 12–15 min; core 75 °C.
Rest 3 min, remove the string and serve 2 rolls with the pan juices.
95f114f2.st: Raw filled rolls: 0–4 °C, 24 h. Cooked involtini: 0–4 °C, 48 h; −18 °C, 2 months. Regenerate to 75 °C core.

c: Raw loin 2.2 kg → 1.6 kg sliced · Yield ≈ 2200 g

Add garlic, sage, rosemary and hot milk to half height; cover partly; simmer very gently 1 h 15 min, turning, to 68 °C core.
Rest meat 15 min. Milk will curdle: blend the sauce smooth with the lemon zest; reduce to 600 g; season.

2fbd09d7.yl: Yield: 5 portions (1 fish each) · Portion: 640 g

Lay each fish on a large sheet of parchment; add the cherry tomatoes and olives around it.
Pour over the wine and olive oil; fold and seal the parcel tightly.
Bake at 200 °C convection for 15–18 min; core 63 °C at the thickest part.
Open the parcel at the table or pass, and serve at once.
2fbd09d7.st: Raw prepared fish: 0–2 °C, 24 h; −18 °C, 3 months. Cooked to order; not stored.

Sweat the diced onion, carrot and celery in the same pan until soft; add wine and reduce by half.

Cover and braise at 150 °C combi (30% humidity) or 155 °C convection, 2–2.5 h, until the meat comes away from the bone; core 90 °C.

Mix finely chopped parsley, lemon zest and garlic just before service.

c: Trim and square the belly; score the skin lightly if needed.
Pound garlic with salt, both paprikas, pepper and oregano to a paste; loosen with the wine.
Rub the meat evenly; marinate covered at 0–4 °C at least 4 h, ideally 12 h.
Roast on a rack over a drip tray at 150 °C convection for 2–2.5 h, until tender; core ≥ 75 °C.
Raise to 220–230 °C for 10–15 min to form a deep red, crisp crust.
Rest 7–10 min and slice 1–1.5 cm thick.
Serve ≈ 160 g sliced pork warm with a lemon wedge and 40 g crusty bread.
7bf4c0cf.st: Marinating: 0–4 °C, max 12 h. Roast pampanella: 0–4 °C, 72 h; −18 °C, 2 months. Regenerate at 180 °C convection to core 75 °C.

Cover with Chianti; lid on; braise 150 °C 3.5–4 h without browning (the old kiln method), stirring every hour.
Uncover the last 30 min to thicken; add rosemary for 10 min, remove.
Serve on grilled bread or soft polenta.
Portion the swordfish into 14 × 180 g steaks; pat dry and season with the salt. Keep at 0–4 °C until cooking.
Sear in the olive oil over high heat 1–2 min per side; remove.
Sauté the garlic 30 s, add the tomatoes, olives and capers and cook 2 min.
Deglaze with the wine and reduce by half.
Return the fish and cook 3–5 min, basting, until core 63 °C.
Serve at once with the sauce spooned over.
e7c0d63c.st: Raw portioned swordfish: 0–2 °C, 48 h; −18 °C, 3 months. Cooked to order; not stored.

c: Trim and pat the chicken dry; season with salt and pepper and dust lightly with flour.
Heat butter and oil in a sauté pan; sear the chicken until golden on both sides.
Deglaze with the wine; add stock, lemon juice and zest.
Simmer 5–6 min, turning once, until the sauce coats a spoon and the chicken reaches core 75 °C.
Cut carrot, courgette and pepper into julienne.
Blanch the green beans 2 min in boiling salted water; refresh in iced water and drain.
Sauté all vegetables in very hot oil 3–4 min so they stay crisp; season.
Slice or plate the chicken whole, spoon over the lemon sauce and arrange the vegetables alongside. Serve at ≥ 63 °C.
a4f9554a.st: Raw prepped chicken: 0–4 °C, 24 h. Cut vegetables: 0–4 °C, 24 h. Cooked chicken in sauce: 0–4 °C, 48 h; −18 °C, 1 month. Cook to order.

Sear in batches in half of the butter and the olive oil until golden, 2–3 min per side; core 75 °C. Keep warm.
Deglaze the pan with the Marsala and reduce to a syrupy glaze.
Off the heat, whisk in the remaining butter.
Return the chicken, coat with the glaze and serve at once.
c044e3ff.st: Raw chicken: 0–4 °C, 48 h. Cooked chicken in sauce: 0–4 °C, 48 h; −18 °C, 2 months. Regenerate to 75 °C core.

Sweat onion and garlic in the same pan; add wine and reduce 2–3 min.
Add tomatoes and herbs; return the chicken.
Simmer covered on low heat 35–45 min (or 160 °C convection, covered) to core 75 °C.
If the sauce is thin, reduce on high heat 4–6 min. Season.

0aea3d6c.yl: Yield: 6 portions (½ chicken each) · Portion: 440 g

Split the chickens along the backbone, flatten and remove the rib bones; you get 6 halves.
Rub with the garlic, chilli and olive oil; marinate for 2–12 h at 0–4 °C.
Season with the salt just before cooking.
Grill skin side down under a weight on a medium-hot grill for 12–15 min, turn and grill a further 10–15 min (or finish at 200 °C convection); core 75 °C at the thigh.
Rest 3 min, squeeze over the juice of half the lemons and serve with the remaining lemon in wedges.
0aea3d6c.st: Raw chicken in marinade: 0–4 °C, max 24 h. Cooked chicken: 0–4 °C, 48 h; −18 °C, 2 months. Regenerate to 75 °C core.

c: Raw chicken 2.5 kg → 1.8 kg; peppers 1.6 kg → 1.0 kg · Yield ≈ 3400 g
Season chicken; brown skin side down in oil 8 min; remove.
Same pan: diced prosciutto, onion, garlic 5 min; peppers in 3 cm strips, 8 min.
Return chicken; white wine, reduce; crushed tomatoes and marjoram/oregano.
Cover; simmer 35–40 min to 80 °C core at the bone; uncover 10 min to thicken.

a0f29d65.yl: Yield: 10 portions · Portion: 2 slices 200 g + 80 g sauce
c: Soak crustless bread in milk; squeeze; mix with meats, eggs, Parmesan, parsley, garlic, seasoning; 2 min to bind.
Spread on baking paper 2 cm; ham and provola in the centre; roll into 2 logs; close the ends.
